request.text:
Matt Pocock walks through his "improve codebase architecture" Claude skill — from the skills repo at 41.5k stars — running it live on his 1,500-commit effect.ts course-video-manager repo to find shallow modules and turn one duplicated ordering rule into a single deep module, framed by a glossary of module/interface/depth/seam/adapter/locality/leverage.

Half the runtime is a vocabulary lesson: module, interface vs implementation, deep vs shallow modules, depth ("behavior a caller can exercise per unit of interface"), seams (where interfaces meet, and where you mock and test), adapters from hexagonal architecture (a real clock vs a fake clock satisfying the same seam), and the two payoffs — locality for maintainers, leverage for callers — all traced back to John Ousterhout's A Philosophy of Software Design. Pocock then opens a fresh Claude session in his course video manager repo, disables auto mode (it breaks human-in-the-loop flows), and runs the skill, which explores the codebase and returns six deepening opportunities. He picks one where a clip-insertion-point rule has two parallel implementations — frontend and backend — with an untested seam between them, and the skill moves into a grilling session of design questions, then proposes a concrete module shape with a sketched TypeScript interface. The output can be piped through to-PRD or to-issues so an AFK agent picks it up. His framing: the agent is a tactical programmer, you are the strategic one, so run this every couple of days and never expect it to be hands-off.
